## General

## 1.1 Attention is drawn in particular to the following Parts of the Civil Procedure Rules:

# Part 1 The overriding objective

[Part 1 The overriding objective] Section I of Part 3 The court’s case management powers

# Part 26 Case management – preliminary stage

# Part 31 Disclosure and inspection of documents

# Part 32 to 34 Evidence

# Part 35 Experts and assessors

[Part 35 Experts and assessors] and to the practice directions which relate to those Parts. ## Case management in the Royal Courts of Justice

[Part 35 Experts and assessors > Case management in the Royal Courts of Justice] 2.1 This part of the practice direction applies to claims begun by claim form issued in the Central Office or Chancery Chambers in the Royal Courts of Justice. ## 2.2 A claim with an estimated value of less than £100,000 will generally, unless:

[Part 35 Experts and assessors > 2.2 A claim with an estimated value of less than £100,000 will generally, unless:] (a) it is required by an enactment to be tried in the High Court,

[Part 35 Experts and assessors > 2.2 A claim with an estimated value of less than £100,000 will generally, unless:] (b) it falls within a specialist list, or

[Part 35 Experts and assessors > 2.2 A claim with an estimated value of less than £100,000 will generally, unless:] (c) it falls within one of the categories specified in 2.6 below or is otherwise within the criteria of article 7(5) of the High Court and County Courts Jurisdiction Order 1991,

[Part 35 Experts and assessors > 2.2 A claim with an estimated value of less than £100,000 will generally, unless:] be transferred to a county court. [Part 35 Experts and assessors > 2.2 A claim with an estimated value of less than £100,000 will generally, unless:] 2.3 Paragraph 2.2 is without prejudice to the power of the court in accordance with Part 30 to transfer to a county court a claim with an estimated value that exceeds £100,000. [Part 35 Experts and assessors > 2.2 A claim with an estimated value of less than £100,000 will generally, unless:] 2.4 The decision to transfer may be made at any stage in the proceedings but should, subject to paragraph 2.5, be made as soon as possible and in any event not later than the date for the filing of pre-trial check lists (listing questionnaires). [Part 35 Experts and assessors > 2.2 A claim with an estimated value of less than £100,000 will generally, unless:] 2.5 If an application is made under rule 3.4 (striking out) or under Part 24 (summary judgment) or under Part 25 (interim remedies), it will usually be convenient for the application to be dealt with before a decision to transfer is taken. [Part 35 Experts and assessors > 2.2 A claim with an estimated value of less than £100,000 will generally, unless:] 2.6 Each party should state in his directions questionnaire whether he considers the claim should be managed and tried at the Royal Courts of Justice and, if so, why. Claims suitable for trial in the Royal Courts of Justice include:

[Part 35 Experts and assessors > 2.2 A claim with an estimated value of less than £100,000 will generally, unless:] (1) professional negligence claims,

[Part 35 Experts and assessors > 2.2 A claim with an estimated value of less than £100,000 will generally, unless:] (2) Fatal Accident Act claims,

[Part 35 Experts and assessors > 2.2 A claim with an estimated value of less than £100,000 will generally, unless:] (3) fraud or undue influence claims,

[Part 35 Experts and assessors > 2.2 A claim with an estimated value of less than £100,000 will generally, unless:] (4) defamation claims,

[Part 35 Experts and assessors > 2.2 A claim with an estimated value of less than £100,000 will generally, unless:] (5) claims for malicious prosecution or false imprisonment,

[Part 35 Experts and assessors > 2.2 A claim with an estimated value of less than £100,000 will generally, unless:] (6) claims against the police,

[Part 35 Experts and assessors > 2.2 A claim with an estimated value of less than £100,000 will generally, unless:] (7) contentious probate claims. [Part 35 Experts and assessors > 2.2 A claim with an estimated value of less than £100,000 will generally, unless:] Such claims may fall within the criteria of article 7(5) of the High Court and County Courts Jurisdiction Order 1991. [Part 35 Experts and assessors > 2.2 A claim with an estimated value of less than £100,000 will generally, unless:] 2.6A If the claim falls within a specialist list or area of work (i.e. Chancery, Commercial/Mercantile, or TCC), and concerns a dispute arising in a region outside London, the parties are required to explain in their directions questionnaire how and why the case is not suitable to be heard in the appropriate regional specialist court. Those regional specialist court centres have been set up to deal with appropriate cases out of London, so the parties will need to state in detail why, despite the availability of a regional specialist court, they wish the case to be heard in London. ## 2.7 Attention is drawn to Practice Direction 30. ## Case management – general provisions

## 3.1

[Part 35 Experts and assessors > 3.1] (1) Case management of a claim which is proceeding at the Royal Courts of Justice will be undertaken there. [Part 35 Experts and assessors > 3.1] (2)

[Part 35 Experts and assessors > 3.1] (a) Case management of any other claim which has been allocated to the multi-track will normally be undertaken at a Civil Trial Centre. [Part 35 Experts and assessors > 3.1] (b) Practice Direction 26 provides for what will happen in the case of a claim which is issued in or transferred to a court which is not a Civil Trial Centre. ## 3.2 The hallmarks of the multi-track are:

[Part 35 Experts and assessors > 3.2 The hallmarks of the multi-track are:] (1) the ability of the court to deal with cases of widely differing values and complexity, and

[Part 35 Experts and assessors > 3.2 The hallmarks of the multi-track are:] (2) the flexibility given to the court in the way it will manage a case in a way appropriate to its particular needs. ## 3.3

[Part 35 Experts and assessors > 3.3] (1) On allocating a claim to the multi-track the court may give directions without a hearing, including fixing a trial date or a period in which the trial will take place,

[Part 35 Experts and assessors > 3.3] (2) Alternatively, whether or not it fixes a trial date or period, it may either –

[Part 35 Experts and assessors > 3.3] (a) give directions for certain steps to be taken and fix a date for a case management conference or a pre-trial review to take place after they have been taken, or

[Part 35 Experts and assessors > 3.3] (b) fix a date for a case management conference. [Part 35 Experts and assessors > 3.3] (3) Attention is drawn to rule 29.2(2) which requires the court to fix a trial date or period as soon as practicable. [Part 35 Experts and assessors > 3.3] 3.4 The court may give or vary directions at any hearing which may take place on the application of a party or of its own initiative. [Part 35 Experts and assessors > 3.3] 3.5 When any hearing has been fixed it is the duty of the parties to consider what directions the court should be asked to give and to make any application that may be appropriate to be dealt with then. [Part 35 Experts and assessors > 3.3] 3.6 The court will hold a hearing to give directions whenever it appears necessary or desirable to do so, and where this happens because of the default of a party or his legal representative it will usually impose a sanction. [Part 35 Experts and assessors > 3.3] 3.7 When the court fixes a hearing to give directions it will give the parties at least 3 days’ notice of the hearing unless rule 29.7 applies (7 days’ notice to be given in the case of a pre-trial review). [Part 35 Experts and assessors > 3.3] 3.8 Where a party needs to apply for a direction of a kind not included in the case management timetable which has been set (for example to amend his statement of case or for further information to be given by another party) he must do so as soon as possible so as to minimise the need to change that timetable. [Part 35 Experts and assessors > 3.3] 3.9 Courts will make arrangements to ensure that applications and other hearings are listed promptly to avoid delay in the conduct of cases. ## 3.10

[Part 35 Experts and assessors > 3.10] (1) Case management will generally be dealt with by:

[Part 35 Experts and assessors > 3.10] (a) a Master in cases proceeding in the Royal Courts of Justice,

[Part 35 Experts and assessors > 3.10] (b) a district judge in cases proceeding in a District Registry of the High Court, and

[Part 35 Experts and assessors > 3.10] (c) a district judge or a Circuit Judge in cases proceeding in a county court. [Part 35 Experts and assessors > 3.10] (2) A Master or a district judge may consult and seek the directions of a judge of a higher level about any aspect of case management. [Part 35 Experts and assessors > 3.10] (3) A member of the court staff who is dealing with the listing of a hearing may seek the directions of any judge about any aspect of that listing. ## Case management – consideration of periodical payments

[Part 35 Experts and assessors > Case management – consideration of periodical payments] 3A Attention is drawn to Practice Direction 41B supplementing Part 41 and in particular to the direction that in a personal injury claim the court should consider and indicate to the parties as soon as practicable whether periodical payments or a lump sum is likely to be the more appropriate form for all or part of an award of damages for future pecuniary loss. ## Directions on allocation

## 4.1 Attention is drawn to the court’s duties under Rule 29.2. [Part 35 Experts and assessors > 4.1 Attention is drawn to the court’s duties under Rule 29.2.] 4.2 The court will seek to tailor its directions to the needs of the case and the steps which the parties have already taken to prepare the case of which it is aware. In particular it will have regard to the extent to which Practice Direction (Pre-Action Conduct) or any pre-action protocol has or (as the case may be) has not been complied with. [Part 35 Experts and assessors > 4.1 Attention is drawn to the court’s duties under Rule 29.2.] 4.3 At this stage the court’s first concern will be to ensure that the issues between the parties are identified and that the necessary evidence is prepared and disclosed. [Part 35 Experts and assessors > 4.1 Attention is drawn to the court’s duties under Rule 29.2.] 4.4 The court may have regard to any document filed by a party with his directions questionnaire containing further information, provided that the document states either that its contents has been agreed with every other party or that it has been served on every other party, and when it was served. [Part 35 Experts and assessors > 4.1 Attention is drawn to the court’s duties under Rule 29.2.] 4.5 On the allocation of a claim to the multi-track the court will consider whether it is desirable or necessary to hold a case management conference straight away, or whether it is appropriate instead to give directions on its own initiative. [Part 35 Experts and assessors > 4.1 Attention is drawn to the court’s duties under Rule 29.2.] 4.6 Attention is drawn to rule 29.4, which provides that parties must endeavour to agree appropriate directions for the management of the proceedings, and requires the agreed directions or proposals to be submitted to the court within a specified time period. ## 4.7

[Part 35 Experts and assessors > 4.7] (1) To obtain the court’s approval the agreed directions must –

[Part 35 Experts and assessors > 4.7] (a) set out a timetable by reference to calendar dates for the taking of steps for the preparation of the case,

[Part 35 Experts and assessors > 4.7] (b) include a date or a period (the trial period) when it is proposed that the trial will take place,

[Part 35 Experts and assessors > 4.7] (c) include provision about disclosure of documents, and

[Part 35 Experts and assessors > 4.7] (d) include provision about both factual and expert evidence. [Part 35 Experts and assessors > 4.7] (2) The court will scrutinise the timetable carefully and in particular will be concerned to see that any proposed date or period for the trial and (if provided for) for a case management conference is no later than is reasonably necessary. [Part 35 Experts and assessors > 4.7] (3) The provision in (1)(c) above may –

[Part 35 Experts and assessors > 4.7] (a) limit disclosure to standard disclosure or less than that, and/or

[Part 35 Experts and assessors > 4.7] (b) direct that disclosure will take place by the supply of copy documents without a list, but it must in that case say either that the parties must serve a disclosure statement with the copies or that they have agreed to disclose in that way without such a statement. [Part 35 Experts and assessors > 4.7] (4) The provision in (1)(d) about expert evidence may be to the effect that none is required. ## 4.8 Directions agreed by the parties should also where appropriate contain provisions about:

[Part 35 Experts and assessors > 4.8 Directions agreed by the parties should also where appropriate contain provisions about:] (1) the filing of any reply or amended statement of case that may be required,

[Part 35 Experts and assessors > 4.8 Directions agreed by the parties should also where appropriate contain provisions about:] (2) dates for the service of requests for further information under Practice Direction 18 and of questions to experts under rule 35.6 and by when they are to be dealt with,

[Part 35 Experts and assessors > 4.8 Directions agreed by the parties should also where appropriate contain provisions about:] (3) the disclosure of evidence,

[Part 35 Experts and assessors > 4.8 Directions agreed by the parties should also where appropriate contain provisions about:] (4) the use of a single joint expert, or in cases where it is not agreed, the exchange of expert evidence (including whether exchange is to be simultaneous or sequential) and without prejudice discussions between experts. [Part 35 Experts and assessors > 4.8 Directions agreed by the parties should also where appropriate contain provisions about:] (see paragraphs 6, 7 and 9 of Practice Direction 35)

[Part 35 Experts and assessors > 4.8 Directions agreed by the parties should also where appropriate contain provisions about:] 4.9 If the court does not approve the agreed directions filed by the parties but decides that it will give directions of its own initiative without fixing a case management conference, it will take them into account in deciding what directions to give. [Part 35 Experts and assessors > 4.8 Directions agreed by the parties should also where appropriate contain provisions about:] 4.10 Where the court is to give directions on its own initiative without holding a case management conference and it is not aware of any steps taken by the parties other than the exchange of statements of case, its general approach will be:

[Part 35 Experts and assessors > 4.8 Directions agreed by the parties should also where appropriate contain provisions about:] (1) to give directions for the filing and service of any further information required to clarify either party’s case,

[Part 35 Experts and assessors > 4.8 Directions agreed by the parties should also where appropriate contain provisions about:] (2) to direct standard disclosure between the parties,

[Part 35 Experts and assessors > 4.8 Directions agreed by the parties should also where appropriate contain provisions about:] (3) to direct the disclosure of witness statements by way of simultaneous exchange,

[Part 35 Experts and assessors > 4.8 Directions agreed by the parties should also where appropriate contain provisions about:] (4) to give directions for a single joint expert on any appropriate issue unless there is a good reason not to do so,

[Part 35 Experts and assessors > 4.8 Directions agreed by the parties should also where appropriate contain provisions about:] (5) unless paragraph 4.11 (below) applies, to direct disclosure of experts’ reports by way of simultaneous exchange on those issues where a single joint expert is not directed,

[Part 35 Experts and assessors > 4.8 Directions agreed by the parties should also where appropriate contain provisions about:] (6) if experts’ reports are not agreed, to direct a discussion between experts for the purpose set out in rule 35.12(1) and the preparation of a statement under rule 35.12(3),

[Part 35 Experts and assessors > 4.8 Directions agreed by the parties should also where appropriate contain provisions about:] (7) to list a case management conference to take place after the date for compliance with those directions,

[Part 35 Experts and assessors > 4.8 Directions agreed by the parties should also where appropriate contain provisions about:] (8) to specify a trial period; and

[Part 35 Experts and assessors > 4.8 Directions agreed by the parties should also where appropriate contain provisions about:] (9) in such cases as the court thinks appropriate, the court may give directions ordering or encouraging the parties to engage in alternative dispute resolution (ADR). Such directions may be, for example, in the following terms:

[Part 35 Experts and assessors > 4.8 Directions agreed by the parties should also where appropriate contain provisions about:] The parties shall by [date] consider whether the case is capable of resolution by ADR. If any party considers that the case is unsuitable for resolution by ADR, that party shall be prepared to justify that decision at the conclusion of the trial, should the judge consider that such means of resolution were appropriate, when he is considering the appropriate costs order to make. [Part 35 Experts and assessors > 4.8 Directions agreed by the parties should also where appropriate contain provisions about:] The party considering the case unsuitable for ADR shall, not less than 28 days before the commencement of the trial, file with the court a witness statement without prejudice save as to costs, giving reasons upon which they rely for saying that the case was unsuitable. [Part 35 Experts and assessors > 4.8 Directions agreed by the parties should also where appropriate contain provisions about:] 4.11 If it appears that expert evidence will be required both on issues of liability and on the amount of damages, the court may direct that the exchange of those reports that relate to liability will be exchanged simultaneously but that those relating to the amount of damages will be exchanged sequentially. ## 4.12

[Part 35 Experts and assessors > 4.12] (1) If it appears to the court that it cannot properly give directions on its own initiative and no agreed directions have been filed which it can approve, the court will direct a case management conference to be listed. [Part 35 Experts and assessors > 4.12] (2) The conference will be listed as promptly as possible. [Part 35 Experts and assessors > 4.12] 4.13 Where the court is proposing on its own initiative to make an order under rule 35.7 (which gives the court power to direct that evidence on a particular issue is to be given by a single expert) or under rule 35.15 (which gives the court power to appoint an assessor), the court must, unless the parties have consented in writing to the order, list a case management conference. ## Case management conferences

## 5.1 The court will at any case management conference:

[Part 35 Experts and assessors > 5.1 The court will at any case management conference:] (1) review the steps which the parties have taken in the preparation of the case, and in particular their compliance with any directions that the court may have given,

[Part 35 Experts and assessors > 5.1 The court will at any case management conference:] (2) decide and give directions about the steps which are to be taken to secure the progress of the claim in accordance with the overriding objective, and

[Part 35 Experts and assessors > 5.1 The court will at any case management conference:] (3) ensure as far as it can that all agreements that can be reached between the parties about the matters in issue and the conduct of the claim are made and recorded. ## 5.2

[Part 35 Experts and assessors > 5.2] (1) Rule 29.3(2) provides that where a party has a legal representative, a representative familiar with the case and with sufficient authority to deal with any issues that are likely to arise must attend case management conferences and pre-trial reviews. [Part 35 Experts and assessors > 5.2] (2) That person should be someone who is personally involved in the conduct of the case, and who has the authority and information to deal with any matter which may reasonably be expected to be dealt with at such a hearing, including the fixing of the timetable, the identification of issues and matters of evidence. [Part 35 Experts and assessors > 5.2] (3) Where the inadequacy of the person attending or of his instructions leads to the adjournment of a hearing, the court will expect to make a wasted costs order. ## 5.3 The topics the court will consider at a case management conference are likely to include:

[Part 35 Experts and assessors > 5.3 The topics the court will consider at a case management conference are likely to include:] (1) whether the claimant has made clear the claim he is bringing, in particular the amount he is claiming, so that the other party can understand the case he has to meet,

[Part 35 Experts and assessors > 5.3 The topics the court will consider at a case management conference are likely to include:] (2) whether any amendments are required to the claim, a statement of case or any other document,

[Part 35 Experts and assessors > 5.3 The topics the court will consider at a case management conference are likely to include:] (3) what disclosure of documents, if any, is necessary,

[Part 35 Experts and assessors > 5.3 The topics the court will consider at a case management conference are likely to include:] (4) what expert evidence is reasonably required in accordance with rule 35.1 and how and when that evidence should be obtained and disclosed,

[Part 35 Experts and assessors > 5.3 The topics the court will consider at a case management conference are likely to include:] (5) what factual evidence should be disclosed,

[Part 35 Experts and assessors > 5.3 The topics the court will consider at a case management conference are likely to include:] (6) what arrangements should be made about the giving of clarification or further information and the putting of questions to experts, and

[Part 35 Experts and assessors > 5.3 The topics the court will consider at a case management conference are likely to include:] (7) whether it will be just and will save costs to order a split trial or the trial of one or more preliminary issues. [Part 35 Experts and assessors > 5.3 The topics the court will consider at a case management conference are likely to include:] 5.4 In all cases the court will set a timetable for the steps it decides are necessary to be taken. These steps may include the holding of a case management conference or a pre-trial review, and the court will be alert to perform its duty to fix a trial date or period as soon as it can. ## 5.5

[Part 35 Experts and assessors > 5.5] (1) The court will not at this stage give permission to use expert evidence unless it can identify each expert by name or field in its order and say whether his evidence is to be given orally or by the use of his report. [Part 35 Experts and assessors > 5.5] (2) A party who obtains expert evidence before obtaining a direction about it does so at his own risk as to costs, except where he obtained the evidence in compliance with a pre-action protocol. ## 5.6 To assist the court, the parties and their legal advisers should:

[Part 35 Experts and assessors > 5.6 To assist the court, the parties and their legal advisers should:] (1) ensure that all documents that the court is likely to ask to see (including witness statements and experts’ reports) are brought to the hearing,

[Part 35 Experts and assessors > 5.6 To assist the court, the parties and their legal advisers should:] (2) consider whether the parties should attend,

[Part 35 Experts and assessors > 5.6 To assist the court, the parties and their legal advisers should:] (3) consider whether a case summary will be useful, and

[Part 35 Experts and assessors > 5.6 To assist the court, the parties and their legal advisers should:] (4) consider what orders each wishes to be made and give notice of them to the other parties. ## 5.7

[Part 35 Experts and assessors > 5.7] (1) A case summary:

[Part 35 Experts and assessors > 5.7] (a) should be designed to assist the court to understand and deal with the questions before it,

[Part 35 Experts and assessors > 5.7] (b) should set out a brief chronology of the claim, the issues of fact which are agreed or in dispute and the evidence needed to decide them,

[Part 35 Experts and assessors > 5.7] (c) should not normally exceed 500 words in length, and

[Part 35 Experts and assessors > 5.7] (d) should be prepared by the claimant and agreed with the other parties if possible. ## 5.8

[Part 35 Experts and assessors > 5.8] (1) Where a party wishes to obtain an order not routinely made at a case management conference and believes that his application will be opposed, he should issue and serve the application in time for it to be heard at the case management conference. [Part 35 Experts and assessors > 5.8] (2) If the time allowed for the case management conference is likely to be insufficient for the application to be heard he should inform the court at once so that a fresh date can be fixed. [Part 35 Experts and assessors > 5.8] (3) A costs sanction may be imposed on a party who fails to comply with sub-paragraph (1) or (2). [Part 35 Experts and assessors > 5.8] 5.9 At a case management conference the court may also consider whether the case ought to be tried by a High Court judge or by a judge who specialises in that type of claim and how that question will be decided. In that case the claim may need to be transferred to another court. ## Variation of directions

## 6.1 This paragraph deals with the procedure to be adopted:

[Part 35 Experts and assessors > 6.1 This paragraph deals with the procedure to be adopted:] (1) where a party is dissatisfied with a direction given by the court,

[Part 35 Experts and assessors > 6.1 This paragraph deals with the procedure to be adopted:] (2) where the parties have agreed about changes they wish made to the directions given, or

[Part 35 Experts and assessors > 6.1 This paragraph deals with the procedure to be adopted:] (3) where a party wishes to apply to vary a direction. ## 6.2

[Part 35 Experts and assessors > 6.2] (1) It is essential that any party who wishes to have a direction varied takes steps to do so as soon as possible. [Part 35 Experts and assessors > 6.2] (2) The court will assume for the purposes of any later application that a party who did not appeal, and who made no application to vary within 14 days of service of the order containing the directions, was content that they were correct in the circumstances then existing. ## 6.3

[Part 35 Experts and assessors > 6.3] (1) Where a party is dissatisfied with a direction given or other order made by the court he may appeal or apply to the court for it to reconsider its decision. [Part 35 Experts and assessors > 6.3] (2) Unless paragraph 6.4 applies, a party should appeal if the direction was given or the order was made at a hearing at which he was present, or of which he had due notice. [Part 35 Experts and assessors > 6.3] (3) In any other case he should apply to the court to reconsider its decision. [Part 35 Experts and assessors > 6.3] (4) If an application is made for the court to reconsider its decision:

[Part 35 Experts and assessors > 6.3] (a) it will usually be heard by the judge who gave the directions or another judge of the same level,

[Part 35 Experts and assessors > 6.3] (b) the court will give all parties at least 3 days notice of the hearing, and

[Part 35 Experts and assessors > 6.3] (c) the court may confirm its directions or make a different order. [Part 35 Experts and assessors > 6.3] 6.4 Where there has been a change in the circumstances since the order was made the court may set aside or vary a direction it has given. It may do so on application or on its own initiative. ## 6.5 Where the parties agree about changes they wish made to the directions given:

[Part 35 Experts and assessors > 6.5 Where the parties agree about changes they wish made to the directions given:] (1) If rule 2.11 (variation by agreement of a date set by the court for doing any act other than those stated in the note to that rule), rule 3.8(4) (extensions of time by written agreement in circumstances within rule 3.8(3)) or rule 31.5, 31.10(8) or 31.13 (agreements about disclosure) applies the parties need not file the written agreement. [Part 35 Experts and assessors > 6.5 Where the parties agree about changes they wish made to the directions given:] (2)

[Part 35 Experts and assessors > 6.5 Where the parties agree about changes they wish made to the directions given:] (a) In any other case the parties must apply for an order by consent. [Part 35 Experts and assessors > 6.5 Where the parties agree about changes they wish made to the directions given:] (b) The parties must file a draft of the order sought and an agreed statement of the reasons why the variation is sought. [Part 35 Experts and assessors > 6.5 Where the parties agree about changes they wish made to the directions given:] (c) The court may make an order in the agreed terms or in other terms without a hearing, but it may direct that a hearing is to be listed. ## Failure to comply with case management directions

[Part 35 Experts and assessors > Failure to comply with case management directions] 7.1 Where a party fails to comply with a direction given by the court any other party may apply for an order that he must do so or for a sanction to be imposed or both of these. [Part 35 Experts and assessors > Failure to comply with case management directions] 7.2 The party entitled to apply for such an order must do so without delay but should first warn the other party of his intention to do so. [Part 35 Experts and assessors > Failure to comply with case management directions] 7.3 The court may take any such delay into account when it decides whether to make an order imposing a sanction or to grant relief from a sanction imposed by the rules or any other practice direction. ## 7.4

[Part 35 Experts and assessors > 7.4] (1) The court will not allow a failure to comply with directions to lead to the postponement of the trial unless the circumstances are exceptional. [Part 35 Experts and assessors > 7.4] (2) If it is practical to do so the court will exercise its powers in a manner that enables the case to come on for trial on the date or within the period previously set. [Part 35 Experts and assessors > 7.4] (3) In particular the court will assess what steps each party should take to prepare the case for trial, direct that those steps are taken in the shortest possible time and impose a sanction for non-compliance. Such a sanction may, for example, deprive a party of the right to raise or contest an issue or to rely on evidence to which the direction relates. [Part 35 Experts and assessors > 7.4] (4) Where it appears that one or more issues are or can be made ready for trial at the time fixed while others cannot, the court may direct that the trial will proceed on the issues which are then ready, and direct that no costs will be allowed for any later trial of the remaining issues or that those costs will be paid by the party in default. [Part 35 Experts and assessors > 7.4] (5) Where the court has no option but to postpone the trial it will do so for the shortest possible time and will give directions for the taking of the necessary steps in the meantime as rapidly as possible. [Part 35 Experts and assessors > 7.4] (6) Litigants and lawyers must be in no doubt that the court will regard the postponement of a trial as an order of last resort.
